title: Vic Gaspard's playing at the Lyric Theater, his tone and instruments
summary: Gaspard played Lyric Theater with John Robichaud, had a smooth tone, played slide trombone, baritone and bass horn, and was the oldest trombonist in town.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I wonder if you could tell us a little bit more. I'm interested in Vic Gaspar especially since I never got to talk to him or even meet him. Did you hear him with any dance bands much in those days? Oh yeah, there was lots of dance bands. Was he still playing then when you came to town? Oh sure. He's playing. He played at the Lyric Theater. I was in town since 1910. Oh I didn't know. I thought maybe you didn't get here until 1925 or something. No, no, no. Oh you came down early then. Oh I didn't know. Vic Gaspar used to play at the Lyric Theater with John Robichaud.
Yeah, I've heard of that band. John Robichaud. He used to play at the Lyric Theater. He's a good trombone player.

What style did he have? Did he have a big tone? Did he do much sliding? Or was it a rough style or smooth or how? Smooth. He's smooth. Smooth. He used to tell me all the time one good note is better than a thousand bad notes.
Yeah. He's a smooth trombone player.
Good. Did he always play a slide when you knew him or did he ever play the vowel trombone? He played the vowel trombone.

He played the baritone. He played the bass. The bass horn. The big tuba. The big tuba, yeah. He played all that. He didn't play the slide trombone? He played the slide trombone too. Oh he played the slide and the bass horn. Oh he played the slide then? Yes I know he played that. Slide, vowel, and baritone and bass horn. Oh he played the bass horn. He played the bass horn.
When you first got here say 1910 do you remember the first time you heard him was he using the slide then?
He was using the slide up until he died. He went on to the slide. He stuck to the slide.
I wondered if you took up the slide while you were still in town do you know about when he might have taken up the slide trombone or did he play it every time?

He was the oldest trombone player when he started teaching me in town. He was 22 years old playing trombone 22 years when he would take me up. He was the oldest trombone player in town. That was in 1925 then? That was in 1925 he was 22 years old on the trombone.
So he'd been playing since about 1903 then? 1903 or something like that.
1903 something like that. Before we were born. Yeah. Well I was born in 1903. Oh you were born in 1903 then?
I was born in 1905. 1905. Yeah. They look older than you.
Don't go by the looks there though. The Sheik might look older than me too. Yeah I believe he does a little. Sheik born in 1980. Yeah he does look a little older. That's right.
